policies.title: Assembly is not decompilation
policies.text: The whole executable builds from source and is byte-identical, but a function counts as decompiled only when it is C or C++ a programmer could have written. Functions kept as assembly, with inline CPU assembly or with a register pin are shown separately until they are rewritten. Vector-unit assembly that C cannot express is accepted.

policies.title: Names from the developers, not from a model
policies.text: Function, class and member names come from the debug information of the 2014 PS3 E3 build. Each mapping to a PS2 function carries a confidence tier; unproven names keep their address.

policies.title: Adversarial review of hand-written work
policies.text: A separate reviewer that never saw the author's reasoning judges names, types and readability (ACCEPT / CHANGES / REJECT). Only ACCEPT merges.

policies.title: Whole-ELF verification
policies.text: Every merge rebuilds the ELF and compares it byte for byte with SLPM_666.75.

phases.title: A byte-identical build
phases.summary: The whole main executable builds from source and matches the original byte for byte. Most of that matching was done by the zcroker fork, which this project adopted as its base in November 2026.

milestones.title: SLPM_666.75 rebuilt from source
milestones.desc: All 11,509 functions in the table are compiled and linked; the result is identical to the original.

milestones.title: One base instead of two efforts
milestones.desc: The zcroker fork reached a full byte-identical build first. Its source became this project's base, with this project's rules, names, file map and site on top.

milestones.title: Build without Docker
milestones.desc: The same build runs in a no-network sandbox (tools/sandbox.sh).

milestones.title: Knowing what the source is made of
milestones.desc: tools/quality.py classes every function as C/C++, vector-unit assembly, inline assembly, register pin or assembly file.

milestones.title: This progress website
milestones.desc: Regenerated from a verified build on every merge.

phases.title: Real names
phases.summary: Most functions still have address placeholders. The 2014 PS3 debug build has the developers' own names for about 7,600 of them.

milestones.title: Top-tier names applied
milestones.desc: 1,458 names from the tiers that tested 97 to 98 % correct, on top of the 1,700 the registry already had.

milestones.title: Overloads, constructors and destructors
milestones.desc: About 130 top-tier names whose plain identifier is not unique need a naming scheme before they can be applied.

milestones.title: Lower-tier names, checked
milestones.desc: About 3,500 candidates in the tiers that tested 92 to 96 %; each needs a second piece of evidence before it is applied.

milestones.title: Conflicting names resolved
milestones.desc: 86 functions where the registry and the debug build disagree.

milestones.title: Named globals
milestones.desc: About 1,000 global variables matched by how the same functions use them on both platforms.

phases.title: Assembly out, C++ in
phases.summary: About a third of the code is byte-identical only with help: assembly files, inline CPU assembly, register pins, or compiler flags switched per file. Each one is a function still to decompile properly.

milestones.title: Every function classified
milestones.desc: 1,247 functions sit in files where assembly could not yet be attributed to single functions.

milestones.title: Inline CPU assembly rewritten as C++
milestones.desc: 607 functions; much of it is 128-bit copies the compiler generates itself from the right types.

milestones.title: Register pins removed
milestones.desc: 84 functions pin a variable to a register to steer the compiler.

milestones.title: Assembly files decompiled
milestones.desc: 170 functions (79 KB) are still plain assembly, hand-written routines excepted.

milestones.title: One set of compiler flags per library
milestones.desc: Per-file flags that only switch off an optimisation pass are a steering trick; find the real source instead.

phases.title: Readable source
phases.summary: Types, class layouts and the original file structure, so the code reads like the game it is.

milestones.title: Original source files
milestones.desc: The PS3 debug build gives 588 original files; functions move out of src/anon into the file that owned them.

milestones.title: Class layouts checked for PS2
milestones.desc: About 5,900 types from the debug build; the HD version shifted many, so each is checked against PS2 offsets.

milestones.title: Members instead of offsets
milestones.desc: Register-style code and raw offset access rewritten with named members, parameters and locals.

milestones.title: Gate and review on every change
milestones.desc: tools/gate.py and the review brief, adapted to this base.

phases.title: The whole game
phases.summary: Data owned by its files, the overlays, and a behaviour check against the original.

milestones.title: Files own their data
milestones.desc: Linked units already carry their data; the rest still takes data from the original image.

milestones.title: The five overlays
milestones.desc: gumibattle, gumimenu, shop, title and movie; about 1.05 MB in OVL.IMG.

milestones.title: Behaviour harness
milestones.desc: The original and our build run side by side in PCSX2 on the same inputs.
